mathematical_content: termwise identity for each prime p: log (p/(p-1)) = 1/p - (log (1 - 1/p) + 1/p)  (from Real.log_div twice plus ring)
summing over Nat.primesLE ⌊x⌋₊ splits the target into difference of two sums (Finset.sum_congr + Finset.sum_sub_distrib)

the constant T = ∑'_p (log(1-1/p) + 1/p) = B_1 - γ CANCELS EXACTLY because both children state the constant through γ and the same series; hence no decimal approximation of Mertens' constant is needed anywhere in the reduction
strictness comes from the strict reciprocal bound plus the non-strict tail domination
design_note_learned: A two-constant split (decimal constants c for the reciprocal bound and d for the tail) is IMPOSSIBLE: the reciprocal bound is only true for c ≥ B_1 and the tail bound only for d ≥ γ − B_1, while the target needs c + d ≤ γ. So c + d = γ forces c = B_1 exactly. Expressing the constant as γ + the same convergent series removes the problem entirely. This is why both children mention (∑' p : Nat.Primes, log(1-1/p) + 1/p).
